scope: Matched temporal phoneme supervision on paired training windows; development validation only.
hypothesis: Training the encoder to retain teacher phone posteriors can improve near-word discrimination without adding any inference head.
pair_sampling: Eight pairs per training batch replace eight positive and eight TTS-negative slots, fixed seed431 pair permutations, same fixed complete windows in both arms. No original source labels are replaced by teacher classes.
advance: Require matched source schedules, first 16 training batches, representative inputs and validation exposure. Treatment must have zero continuous development events and <=1% worst engine/corpus and engine false fraction, with >=3 recall points over binary control. Use control best recall within the same strict gate, otherwise within a 2% false fraction, otherwise the zero-event control point with minimum worst-group false fraction (ties: highest recall, then lowest threshold). No final scoring or board change without promotion.
limits: 118 training-only pairs, 236 rendered windows. Offline teacher sees each complete training crop. Model-coordinate timestamps are not human phone endpoints. This experiment does not establish independent generalization, acoustic latency or P4 acceptance.
objective: Both arms use identical 118-pair windows with original binary labels and weighted BCE. Only treatment adds gain .01 times teacher/student phoneme KL on the 67 temporal encoder outputs. A 392-class auxiliary head is discarded before export. Frame weights .05+.95*(1-P(blank)) preserve blank learning and emphasize sparse phone spikes.
